name: Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor – Failed Payments & Checkout Readiness
author: Web Plura

sections.description:
WooCommerce checkout can appear available while failed payments, pending orders, webhook configuration gaps, test-mode settings, currency mismatches, or checkout setup issues still affect orders.

Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor reviews local WooCommerce gateway configuration and recent order patterns so administrators can investigate payment failures, pending orders, webhook readiness, and checkout setup from wp-admin.

The Free plugin works locally in WordPress. It does not call payment-provider APIs, capture payments, replay webhooks, refund orders, change order statuses, store provider secret keys, or transmit payment-monitoring data to a remote monitoring service.

Key Payment Checks

Use Payment Gateway Monitor to review supported local signals such as:

  • enabled WooCommerce payment gateway inventory;
  • failed-payment and pending-payment trends;
  • aged pending and paid-but-pending order signals;
  • checkout page assignment, published status, block or shortcode presence, and HTTPS;
  • local webhook configuration signals where detectable;
  • gateway mode, provider/plugin information, and currency mismatch warnings;
  • conditional payment or gateway-fee plugin awareness;
  • test-payment readiness checklist and manual gateway test log;
  • local gateway risk score and WordPress Site Health checks;
  • report history, printable summaries, CSV exports, and JSON exports.

Failed Payments

Failed payments can create support work, lost orders, and unclear checkout troubleshooting. Payment Gateway Monitor reviews recent WooCommerce order statuses and shows failed-order counts, failed-payment rate, trend direction, and gateway-level failed-payment summaries where local order data is available.

These checks help administrators investigate patterns. The plugin does not automatically diagnose every failed payment, fix gateway configuration, retry payments, or contact the payment provider.

Pending and Paid-but-Pending Orders

Pending and on-hold orders can hide checkout or webhook follow-up problems. Payment Gateway Monitor can highlight pending-payment orders, pending or on-hold orders older than 24 hours, and paid-but-pending signals where a local WooCommerce order has a transaction ID but remains pending or on hold.

Paid-but-pending is a local diagnostic signal. It is not confirmation from a payment provider and should be reviewed against order notes, gateway settings, and the provider dashboard before taking action.

Checkout Readiness

Checkout can fail even when products and gateways look enabled. The plugin checks whether WooCommerce has a checkout page assigned, whether that page is published, whether the checkout block or classic shortcode is locally detectable, whether the checkout URL uses HTTPS, and whether at least one gateway is enabled.

Use this before a launch, migration, checkout redesign, or payment-gateway change. It is a readiness review, not an end-to-end transaction test.

Webhook Readiness

Payment Gateway Monitor reviews local gateway settings for webhook-related configuration where the gateway exposes fields that WordPress can inspect. This can help administrators prepare a checklist before contacting a gateway provider or checking a provider dashboard.

The plugin does not verify remote webhook registration, watch live webhook delivery, replay webhook events, or read provider delivery logs.

Gateway Configuration Checks

The plugin reviews WooCommerce payment gateways visible to WordPress. It can show enabled or disabled status, local test or sandbox mode signals, provider family labels where locally detectable, related plugin/version information where available, supported readiness items, wallet/express-checkout HTTPS and currency signals, and currency mismatch warnings.

Provider names may appear only as local gateway labels. Payment Gateway Monitor does not call Stripe, PayPal, WooPayments, or other payment-provider APIs.

Test Payment Readiness

The test-payment checklist helps administrators review prerequisites before manually testing checkout. The included manual gateway test log lets an administrator record a local test date, environment, outcome, next due date, and note for each gateway.

The plugin does not place real or sandbox transactions, charge test cards, simulate provider callbacks, or verify funds. Test results are entered manually by an administrator.

Gateway Risk Score

The gateway risk score summarizes supported local findings from the latest scan, such as failed-payment rate, missing local webhook configuration signals, currency mismatch warnings, enabled gateways in test mode, checkout setup issues, aged pending orders, paid-but-pending signals, and recent failed-payment trend direction.

This score is an operational troubleshooting aid. It is not a payment-provider certification, financial rating, uptime monitor, fraud score, or guarantee that checkout will succeed.

Reports and Exports

Administrators can keep local scan history, review issue and recommendation summaries, print a troubleshooting summary, and export supported data for developer, agency, support, or client handoff.

Supported export workflows include report history CSV, report history JSON, issue CSV, and gateway-readiness CSV.

Site Health Integration

Payment Gateway Monitor adds supported gateway-readiness checks to WordPress Site Health. Site Health can show whether a local scan is missing or stale and whether the latest local scan found important payment gateway or checkout readiness warnings.

This is focused on payment gateway readiness. It is not a complete WooCommerce health monitor.

Local Processing and Privacy

The Free plugin runs included scans, reports, exports, print views, settings, manual test logs, and Site Health checks inside WordPress.

It reads local WooCommerce configuration, payment gateway settings visible to WordPress, and recent order-status patterns. It stores plugin-owned settings, local scan summaries, report history, retention settings, and manual gateway test log records in the WordPress database.

Reports are viewed, printed, or exported manually by an administrator. The plugin does not collect provider secrets, full customer payment details, order notes, provider dashboards, remote delivery logs, or external gateway logs.

Uninstall removes plugin-owned options, legacy plugin-owned options, and the plugin-owned scan table.

Optional Web Plura Services

The WordPress.org package includes the local gateway checks, failed and pending payment review, webhook readiness checklist, manual test log, reports, print views, exports, settings, and Site Health signals described in this readme.

Separately installed or hosted Web Plura services may offer account-backed support, hosted operations, scheduled monitoring, alert policies, cross-site workflows, or team reporting. Those optional services are separate from the included local Free plugin behavior and do not unlock the local features listed here.

Important Limitations

Payment Gateway Monitor helps administrators review supported local signals. It does not guarantee that every failed payment, checkout issue, webhook problem, or gateway configuration issue is found.

The plugin does not call payment-provider APIs, store provider secret keys, process payments, capture payments, refund payments, replay webhooks, automatically contact customers, change WooCommerce order statuses, or fix gateway settings automatically.

The Free plugin is WooCommerce-focused. It does not provide non-WooCommerce payment monitoring.

Resources

  • Product page: https://wplura.com/products/web-plura-payment-gateway-monitor
  • Documentation: https://wplura.com/docs
  • Support: https://wplura.com/support
  • Terms: https://wplura.com/terms
  • Privacy: https://wplura.com/privacy

External Services

This free plugin does not connect to external services for its included local scans, reports, exports, print views, manual test logs, settings, or Site Health checks.

The plugin reads local WooCommerce configuration, payment gateway settings visible to WordPress, and recent order-status patterns. Reports are viewed, printed, or exported manually by the administrator. Payment provider secrets, full customer payment details, order notes, provider dashboards, remote delivery logs, and external gateway logs are not collected by this plugin.

Optional Web Plura services are separate from the Free plugin’s included local operation. If an administrator chooses to use a separate hosted service, review that service’s documentation, terms, privacy policy, and consent controls before sending store data.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the web-plura-payment-gateway-monitor folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor in wp-admin.
  4. Run a local scan.
sections.faq:
Does this require WooCommerce?

Yes. The Free plugin is built for WooCommerce. If WooCommerce is not active, the plugin shows dependency guidance instead of running local gateway scans.

Can it help investigate WooCommerce failed payments?

Yes. It reviews supported local failed-payment counts, rates, trend direction, and gateway-level summaries from recent WooCommerce order data.

Can it find pending-payment orders?

Yes. It can show pending and on-hold order counts, aged pending orders, and gateway-level pending-payment summaries where local WooCommerce order data is available.

What does paid-but-pending mean?

It means a local WooCommerce order is pending or on hold while also having a transaction ID. Treat it as a signal for manual review, not as payment-provider confirmation.

What checkout-readiness checks does it perform?

It checks local signals such as checkout page assignment, page publication status, checkout block or shortcode presence, checkout HTTPS, and enabled gateway availability.

Does it verify webhook delivery with the payment provider?

No. The plugin reviews local webhook-related configuration signals where visible to WordPress. It does not verify remote provider registration or live webhook delivery.

Does it call Stripe, PayPal, WooPayments, or other gateway APIs?

No. Provider names may appear as local gateway labels, but the plugin does not call payment-provider APIs, read provider dashboards, or fetch remote delivery logs.

Does it store payment-provider secret keys?

No. The plugin does not store payment-provider secret keys.

Can it make payments, capture payments, or issue refunds?

No. It is a local readiness and troubleshooting tool. It does not process payments, capture payments, charge cards, refund orders, or simulate provider transactions.

Does it change WooCommerce order statuses?

No. It reports local signals for administrator review and does not automatically change order statuses.

Can it help before changing payment gateways or launching checkout?

Yes. It can create a local readiness report with gateway inventory, checkout surface checks, webhook checklist items, test-payment notes, issue summaries, and exports for a launch, migration, or gateway-change review.

What does the gateway risk score mean?

It is a local score based on supported findings from the latest scan. It is meant to help prioritize troubleshooting, not certify a gateway or guarantee successful payment processing.

Does the Free plugin require a Web Plura Cloud account?

No. Included local scans, reports, print views, exports, manual test logs, settings, and Site Health checks work without Web Plura Cloud, Pro, an account, a subscription, a license, entitlement checks, hosted monitoring, or payment data transmission.

What data leaves my WordPress site?

For included Free features, payment-monitoring scan data does not leave WordPress. Reports are viewed, printed, or exported manually by an administrator.

What data is stored locally?

Depending on use, the plugin stores plugin-owned settings, scan summaries, report history, retention settings, last-scan metadata, and manual gateway test log records in the WordPress database.

Can I export reports?

Yes. Supported exports include report history CSV, report history JSON, issue CSV, and gateway-readiness CSV. A printable summary is also available.

What happens on uninstall?

Uninstall removes plugin-owned options, legacy plugin-owned options, and the plugin-owned scan table.

Are any listed local features restricted?

No. Scan size and retention settings are local performance and storage safeguards, not feature restrictions.
